sections.heading: 14.0 Introduction
sections.title: 14.0 Introduction
sections.text: Energy is the most important requirement of life. All systems require energy to work. The various processes carried out by body, such as movement, growth and reproduction, all require the expenditure of energy. In animals this energy can be obtained only from the food they eat. In the processes of cellular respiration this food energy is made available for the body activities. Aerobic respiration involves the use of oxygen and the production of carbon dioxide. Oxygen enters into animal's body from air or water surrounding it. In the less complex animals the oxygen is absorbed over the entire exposed surface of the body. In higher animals, however, there are special respiratory organs such as gills or lungs. Excess carbon dioxide is usually eliminated from the same organ.

sections.heading: 14.1 PROPERTIES OF RESPIRATORY SURFACES
sections.title: 14.1 PROPERTIES OF RESPIRATORY SURFACES
sections.text:
The area where gaseous exchange with the environment actually takes place is called the respiratory surface. Gaseous exchange takes place in all organisms by the physical process of diffusion. For effective diffusion the respiratory surface must have the following properties.

It must be permeable, so that gases can pass through it.
It must be thin for efficient diffusion, because diffusion is only efficient over distance of 1 mm or less.
It should possess a large surface area so that sufficient amounts of gases are able to be exchanged according to the organism's need.
It should possess a good blood supply.
There should be a good ventilation mechanism to maintain a steep diffusion gradient across the respiratory surface.

sections.heading: 14.2 HUMAN RESPIRATORY SYSTEM
sections.title: 14.2 HUMAN RESPIRATORY SYSTEM
sections.text: Respiratory system provides the fundamental ability to breath. This system consists of nose and nasal cavities, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli in the lungs.

paras.text: Respiratory system provides the fundamental ability to breath. This system consists of nose and nasal cavities, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli in the lungs.

sections.heading: 14.2.1 Nose
sections.title: 14.2.1 Nose
sections.text:
The nose is only externally visible part of the respiratory system. The structure of a human nose is composed of bones, cartilage and fibro fatty tissues. The external feature of a nose depends upon the ethmoid bone and the cartilages.

Fig:14.1 Nasal passage through face

Hairs are present inside the nostrils that help in the filtration of air. Hence, nose hair serve as a defense mechanism against the harmful pathogens and solid particulate matter present in the air. Both the nostrils and nasal cavities are lined by mucous membranes along with cilia. The mucous membrane secretes a sticky substance called mucus. The mucus and cilia filter the air and prevent the entry of foreign particles such as microorganisms, dust and particulate matter inside the respiratory system. The mucus also helps in moistening the air. Cilia move the trapped substances to the pharynx for their removal. Underneath the mucous membrane, there are blood capillaries that help to warm the air to about 30 °C, depending upon the external temperature.

paras.pashto: د پوزې د سوریو دننه وېښتان شته چې د هوا په چاڼولو کې مرسته کوي. نو د پوزې وېښتان په هوا کې د زیانمنو ناروغي جوړوونکو او جامدو ذرو پر وړاندې دفاع کوي. د پوزې سوري او جوفونه له دننه په مخاطي پردو او سیلیا پوښل شوي دي. مخاطي پرده یوه سریښناکه ماده ترشح کوي چې میوکس بلل کېږي. میوکس او سیلیا هوا چاڼوي او د کوچنیو ژوندیو موجوداتو، دوړو او نورو بهرنیو ذرو د تنفسي سیسټم دننه د ننوتلو مخه نیسي. میوکس د هوا په لندولو کې هم مرسته کوي. سیلیا بندې شوې مادې د ایستلو لپاره حلق ته لېږدوي. د مخاطي پردې لاندې د وینې نرۍ رګونه شته چې د بهرني تودوخې سره سم هوا نږدې تر 30 °C پورې تودوي.

sections.heading: 14.2.2 Pharynx
sections.title: 14.2.2 Pharynx
sections.text:
Pharynx is cone-shaped passageway leading from the oral and nasal cavities to the oesophagus and larynx. The pharynx is part of both the digestive and respiratory systems.

For Your Information
The interconnection of the oral and nasal regions is extremely beneficial in humans. It allows them to breathe through either the nose or the mouth and, when medically necessary, allows food to be passed to the esophagus by nasal tubes.

paras.text: Pharynx is cone-shaped passageway leading from the oral and nasal cavities to the oesophagus and larynx. The pharynx is part of both the digestive and respiratory systems.

paras.pashto: حلق مخروط ته ورته لاره ده چې د خولې او پوزې له جوفونو څخه د خوړو نل او حنجرې ته ځي. حلق د هاضمې او تنفس دواړو سیسټمونو برخه ده.

paras.text: For Your Information
paras.urdu: آپ کی معلومات کے لیے
paras.pashto: ستاسو د معلوماتو لپاره

paras.text: The interconnection of the oral and nasal regions is extremely beneficial in humans. It allows them to breathe through either the nose or the mouth and, when medically necessary, allows food to be passed to the esophagus by nasal tubes.
paras.urdu: انسانوں میں منہ اور ناک کے حصوں کا باہمی اتصال بہت مفید ہے۔ یہ انہیں ناک یا منہ سے سانس لینے دیتا ہے اور طبی ضرورت کے وقت ناک کی نالیوں کے ذریعے غذا کو غذائی نالی تک پہنچانے کی سہولت دیتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: په انسانانو کې د خولې او پوزې د برخو خپلمنځي اتصال ډېر ګټور دی. دا هغوی ته د پوزې یا خولې له لارې د ساه اخیستلو اجازه ورکوي او د طبي اړتیا پر مهال د پوزې د نلونو له لارې د خوړو نل ته د خوراک د تېرولو اسانتیا برابروي.

sections.heading: 14.2.3 Larynx
sections.title: 14.2.3 Larynx
sections.text:
Larynx is an organ of complex structure that serves as a dual function: as an air canal to the lungs and controller of its access, and as the organ of voice. The larynx is composed of an external skeleton of cartilage plates that prevents collapse of the structure. The plates are fastened together by membranes and muscle fibers. Two fibrous bands called vocal cords are located in the larynx. The vocal cords are composed of mucous membrane stretched horizontally across the larynx.

Fig: 14. 2 Larynx is the upper part of the respiratory system.

paras.urdu: حنجرہ پیچیدہ ساخت کا عضو ہے جس کے دو کام ہیں: پھیپھڑوں تک ہوا پہنچانے کی گزرگاہ اور اس کے داخلے کا کنٹرول، اور آواز پیدا کرنا۔ حنجرے کا بیرونی ڈھانچہ غضروفی تختیوں سے بنا ہے جو اسے دب کر بند ہونے سے بچاتی ہیں۔ یہ تختیاں جھلیوں اور عضلاتی ریشوں سے ایک دوسرے کے ساتھ جڑی ہیں۔ حنجرے میں دو ریشے دار پٹیاں ہوتی ہیں جنہیں صوتی تار کہتے ہیں۔ صوتی تار مخاطی جھلی سے بنے ہیں جو حنجرے میں افقی طور پر تنی ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: حنجره د پېچلي جوړښت غړی دی چې دوه دندې لري: سږو ته د هوا د تېرېدو لاره او د ننوتلو کنټرول، او د غږ جوړول. د حنجرې بهرنی چوکاټ له غضروفي تختو جوړ دی چې د جوړښت د نړېدو مخه نیسي. تختې د پردو او عضلاتي فایبرونو په وسیله سره تړل شوې دي. په حنجره کې دوه فایبري پټې شته چې غږیز تارونه بلل کېږي. غږیز تارونه له مخاطي پردې جوړ دي چې په حنجره کې په افقي ډول غځېدلې ده.

sections.heading: 14.2.4 Trachea
sections.title: 14.2.4 Trachea
sections.text:
Below the larynx lies the trachea, a tube of 10 to 12 cm long and 2cm wide. Its wall is stiffened by 16 to 20 characteristic horse shoe shape incomplete rings that open towards the back and are embedded in a dense connective tissue. Trachea is lined with ciliated mucus membrane. The trachea serves as passage for air, moistens and warms it while it passes into the lungs, and protects the respiratory surface from an accumulation of foreign particles.

tidbit
Men and women have different vocal cord sizes. This difference in size causes a difference in vocal pitch. Adult males have larger cords and usually low pitched voices.

sections.heading: 14.2.5 Bronchi
sections.title: 14.2.5 Bronchi
sections.text:
The trachea divides into two stem bronchi, one each for the left and right lung. The right bronchus has a larger diameter, and is shorter than the left bronchus. Structure of bronchi closely resembles that of the trachea; however they have small cartilaginous plates to support their walls. The bronchi divide and re-divide forming an airway network in the lungs.

sections.heading: 14.2.6 Bronchioles
sections.title: 14.2.6 Bronchioles
sections.text:
The bronchioles are located at the end of the bronchi and terminate in the alveoli. The bronchioles are approximately 1mm or less in diameter and their walls consist of ciliated cuboidal epithelium and a layer of smooth muscle.

The bronchioles are the first airway branches that do not contain cartilage. They are responsible for controlling air distribution in the lungs. The bronchioles change diameter to either increase or reduce air flow. The bronchioles continue to divide and subdivide deep into the lungs. Eventually the terminal bronchioles open into small collections of air sacs known as alveoli, where the actual exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen occur.

sections.heading: 14.2.7 Alveoli
sections.title: 14.2.7 Alveoli
sections.text:
The alveoli form the gas exchange surface. The wall of each alveolus is only 0.1 μm thick. On its outsides is a dense network of blood capillaries. Lining each alveolus is moist squamous epithelium.

tidbit
There are over 700 million alveoli present in the lungs, representing a total surface area of 70-90m.

This consists of very thin, flattened cells, reducing the distance over which diffusion must occur. Collagen and elastic fibres are also present which allow the alveoli to expand and recoil easily during breathing.

sections.heading: 14.2.8 Lungs
sections.title: 14.2.8 Lungs
sections.text:
Human have two lungs, a right and a left, which are located in the thoracic cavity. Together, the lungs occupy most of the intra thoracic space. The right and left lungs are slightly unequal in size. The right lung represents 56% of the total lung volume and is composed of three lobes, a superior, middle, and inferior lobe. The left lung, smaller in volume because of the asymmetrical position of the heart, has only two lobes. In the thorax the two lungs rest with their bases on the diaphragm, while their apexes extend above the first rib.

Fig:14.4 Capillaries form a network over the surface of alveoli.

Skills — Analyzing and Interpreting
Trace the path of air through different parts of human respiratory tract.

For Your Information
Special cells in the alveolus wall secrete a detergent like chemical on to the inside lining of the alveolus. This is called a surfactant. It lowers the surface tension of the fluid layer lining the alveolus, and thereby reduces the amount of effort needed to breathe in and inflate the lungs. Surfactants also help to kill any bacteria which reach the alveoli.

Each lung is encased in a thin membranous sac called the pleura. It consists of two tough, flexible, transparent pleural membranes. These protect the lungs, stop them leaking air into the thoracic cavity and reduce friction between the lungs and the wall of the thorax.

sections.heading: 14.3 LUNG VOLUMES AND CAPACITIES
sections.title: 14.3 LUNG VOLUMES AND CAPACITIES
sections.text:
Lung volumes and lung capacities refer to the volume of air associated with different phases of the respiratory cycle. The average adult human has a lung capacity of approximately 5 liters but only a small amount of this capacity is used during normal breathing.

Tidal volume is the volume of air exchanged during one breath in and out in quiet breathing. This is about 500 ml
Residual volume is the volume of air remaining in the lungs even after a forcible expiration. This is about 1.5 liter.

sections.heading: 14.4.1 Involuntary control
sections.title: 14.4.1 Involuntary control
sections.text:
Involuntary control of breathing is carried out by a breathing centre located in the medulla oblongata. The ventral portion of the breathing centre acts to increase the rate and depth of inspiration and is called inspiratory centre. The dorsal and lateral portions inhibit inspiration and stimulate expiration and form the expiratory centre.

For Your Information
Oxygen concentration also has an effect on the breathing rate. However, under normal circumstances there is an abundance of oxygen available, and its influence is relatively minor. About 20% decrease in oxygen concentration in the air produce a doubling in breathing rate. Oxygen concentration also has an effect on the breathing rate. However, under normal circumstances there is an abundance of oxygen available, and its influence is relatively minor. About 20% decrease in oxygen concentration in the air produce a doubling in breathing rate.

Skills — Analyzing and Interpreting
Identify different parts of the respiratory system of a dissected frog (dissection would be done by the teacher).

The breathing centre communicates with the intercostal muscles by the intercostals nerves and with the diaphragm by the phrenic nerves. Rhythmic nerve impulses to the diaphragm and intercostal muscles bring about breathing movements. We know that breathing consists of two phases namely breathing in or inspiration and breathing out or expiration.

Inspiration (Inhalation)

In human, inspiration is an active process. During inspiration, the intercostal muscles between the ribs contract and pull the ribs forward and outward, pushing the sternum farther away from the vertebral column. By the contraction of the intercostal muscles and of the diaphragm the size of the thorax as a whole is increased and the pleural cavities within it are, therefore enlarged. Since the pleural cavities are closed, their enlargement tends to create a partial vacuum within them. The lungs are elastic and communicate with the atmosphere through the air passages (trachea, bronchi ). As soon as the pressure around the lungs is lowered, the air rushes into them through the trachea by its own pressure and dilated them. In this way the lungs expand to fill the pleural cavities and the pressure on the inside and outside of the thorax are equalized. Thus the mechanism of human breathing is a suction-pump mechanism. The lungs are made to expand and contract by movements of the ribs and diaphragm.

Fig:14.5 Inhalation and exhalation mechanism.

Expiration (Exhalation)

Expiration in human is normally passive. In severe muscular exercise however, the expiration also becomes active. During expiration, the intercostal muscles of the ribs relax, the ribs move down ward and inward. Thus the size of the chest cavity is reduced from side to side. The sternum comes to its original position, decreasing the size of the chest cavity from front to back or dorso-ventrally. At the same time muscles of the diaphragm relax and so the diaphragm assumes its dome shaped position. Thus the relaxation of the muscles of diaphragm and of the intercostals muscles the size of the thorax as a whole is decreased and the pleural cavities within are, therefore, reduced. This reduction in the size of the thorax exerts pressure on the lungs. The lungs themselves are very elastic and tend to return to their original size. When the lungs are pressed, the foul air inside them is expelled or expiration occurs.

sections.heading: 14.4.2 Voluntary control
sections.title: 14.4.2 Voluntary control
sections.text: Within limits, the rate and depth of breathing are also under voluntary control as is evident by the ability to hold the breath. Voluntary control is also used during forced breathing, speech, singing, sneezing and coughing. During voluntary control impulses originate from the cerebral hemispheres and pass to the breathing centre.

sections.heading: 14.5 MECHANISM OF TRANSPORT OF GASES
sections.title: 14.5 MECHANISM OF TRANSPORT OF GASES
sections.text: Like other materials, respiratory gases are also transported in various regions of the body by means of blood. The blood transports oxygen from the lungs to different tissues and carbon dioxides from tissues to the lungs.

sections.heading: 14.5.1 Transport of oxygen in blood:
sections.title: 14.5.1 Transport of oxygen in blood:
sections.headingPashto: په وینه کې د اکسیجن لېږد
sections.text:
Approximately 97% of oxygen is carried by the red blood cells as oxyhaemoglobin, while 3% is transported as dissolved oxygen in the plasma.

At high partial pressure of oxygen, oxygen binds with haemoglobin. This binding is a reversible reaction that occurs in the alveoli of the lungs in the presence of enzyme carbonic anhydrase. Each molecule of haemoglobin can bind with four molecules of oxygen to form oxyhaemoglobin.

Fig: 14.6 Haemoglobin in red blood cells carry oxygen in the blood.

The ability of haemoglobin to bind with oxygen is called oxygen carrying capacity of blood. The oxygen carrying capacity of blood is directly proportional to the partial pressure of oxygen (PO₂). Maximum oxygen carrying capacity of arterial blood is 20 ml/100 ml of blood (100% saturated) which is achieved at 100 mmHg PO₂.

Fig: 14.7

This is because the amount of haemoglobin is 15 gms/100 ml of blood. Since 1gm Hb can combine with 1.34 ml of O₂, therefore 100 ml blood combines with 20 ml O₂ (100% saturated). Normally each 100 ml of arterial blood contains 19.4 ml O₂ (i.e. it is 97% saturated; PO₂ is 95 mmHg), while 100 ml of venous blood contains 14.4 ml O₂ (i.e. it is 75% saturated; PO₂ is 40 mmHg). Thus, 5 ml of O₂ is released to the tissues by each 100 ml blood.

During exercise, the need of oxygen is greatly increased in the tissues so more oxygen is released by the arterial blood to the tissues. The venous blood that leaves an active tissue has only 4.4 ml O₂ per 100 ml of blood (20% saturated; PO₂ is 18 mmHg). Compared to carbon dioxide, oxygen is relatively insoluble in the blood, therefore a small amount of O₂ is transported in dissolved state in the plasma. Normally each 100 ml blood contain 0.29 ml O₂ (PO₂ is 95 mmHg) and this capacity may increase up to 0.3 ml/100 ml blood at 100 mmHg PO₂.

Fig: 14. 8

While the 100 ml of venous blood has 0.12 ml of dissolved O₂ (PO₂ is 40 mmHg). Thus, 0.17 ml of O₂ is transported by each 100 ml blood through the tissues per cycle in the dissolved state.

sections.heading: 14.5.2 Transport of Carbon dioxide:
sections.title: 14.5.2 Transport of Carbon dioxide:
sections.text:
Carbon dioxide is transported in the blood in three main ways i.e. in the form of bicarbonate ions, in the form of carboxyhaemoglobin and dissolved in plasma.

(i) As bicarbonate ions:

Approximately 70% of carbon dioxide is carried in the blood as bicarbonate ions. Carbon dioxide diffuses into the blood and combines with water to form carbonic acid in the presence of enzyme carbonic anhydrase. The chemical reaction can be depicted as follows:

Carbonic acid, H₂CO₃ is an unstable compound and dissociate to form hydrogen ions and bicarbonate ions.

Accumulation of H⁺ ions increases acidity in the blood, i.e. it leads to the decrease in pH. This does not occur since haemoglobin buffers the hydrogen formed. The hydrogen ion readily associates with oxyhaemoglobin to form haemoglobinic acid and oxygen is released to the tissue.

From inside of the erythrocytes negatively charged HCO₃⁻ ions diffuse to the plasma. This is balanced by the diffusion of chloride ions, Cl-, in the opposite direction. This is achieved by special bicarbonate-chloride carrier proteins that exist in the RBC membrane. This protein moves the two ions in opposite directions, maintaining the balance of ions on either side. This is called the chloride shifts or Hamburger's phenomenon.

Fig: 14. 9 Mechanism of transport of carbondioxide.

The chloride ions that enters the RBC combine with potassium (K+) to form potassium chloride, whereas bicarbonate ions in the blood plasma combines with Na+ to form sodium bicarbonates.

Skills — Initiating and Planning
Examine some sheep's lungs obtained from butcher's shop.

For Your Information
All vertebrates use the haemoglobin as respiratory pigment that transports gases in the body, whereas invertebrates have respiratory pigments like haemocyanin (in Molluscs), haemoerythrin (in some marine animals) and chlorocruorin (in annelids). Haemoglobin is bright red when oxygenated, and dark red when deoxygenated, oxygenated haemocyanin is blue in color, deoxygenated is almost colourless. Oxygenated chlorocruorin turns green where oxygenated haemoerythrin is a violet to pink colour, and colourless when deoxygenated. Do you think why human blood is of red colour? In colored diagrams of human circulatory system, venous blood is generally represented by blue color. Do you think our venous blood is really of blue color?

The blood pH is thus maintained at approximately 7.4 by the buffer mechanism that exists in blood. Transport of CO₂ depends on the partial pressure of CO₂. In case the partial pressure of CO₂ is higher in tissues than blood, the reaction proceeds as drawn above. However, in case the partial pressure of CO₂ is higher in the blood than outside of the blood (as in case of the lungs), the equation reverse and bicarbonate ions with hydrogen ion to release carbon dioxide and water.

(ii) As Carbaminohaemoglobin:

About 23% of carbon dioxide is carried as carbaminohaemoglobin. CO₂ combines with the globin part of haemoglobin. The reaction depends upon the partial pressure of CO₂. When the PCO₂ is higher in the tissues than blood, formation of carbaminohaemoglobin occurs. When the PCO₂ is higher in the blood than tissues as in case of lungs, carbaminohaemoglobin releases its CO₂.

(iii) As dissolved CO₂ in plasma:

Only 7% of carbon dioxide is carried this way. This is rather inefficient way to carry carbon dioxide, but it does occur.

When the PCO₂ is higher in the blood than tissues as in case of lungs, carbaminohaemoglobin releases its CO₂.
paras.urdu: تقریباً 23% کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کاربامینو ہیموگلوبن کی صورت میں منتقل ہوتی ہے۔ CO₂ ہیموگلوبن کے گلوبن حصے سے جڑتی ہے۔ تعامل CO₂ کے جزوی دباؤ پر منحصر ہوتا ہے۔ جب بافتوں میں PCO₂ خون سے زیادہ ہو تو کاربامینو ہیموگلوبن بنتا ہے۔ جب خون میں PCO₂ بافتوں سے زیادہ ہو، جیسا کہ پھیپھڑوں میں، تو کاربامینو ہیموگلوبن اپنی CO₂ خارج کرتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: نږدې 23% کاربن ډای اکسایډ د کاربامینو هیموګلوبین په بڼه لېږدول کېږي. CO₂ د هیموګلوبین له ګلوبین برخې سره یوځای کېږي. تعامل د CO₂ په جزوي فشار پورې اړه لري. کله چې په نسجونو کې PCO₂ له وینې لوړ وي، کاربامینو هیموګلوبین جوړېږي. کله چې په وینه کې PCO₂ له نسجونو لوړ وي، لکه په سږو کې، کاربامینو هیموګلوبین خپل CO₂ خوشې کوي.

paras.text: Only 7% of carbon dioxide is carried this way. This is rather inefficient way to carry carbon dioxide, but it does occur.

sections.heading: 14.6 RESPIRATORY PIGMENTS
sections.title: 14.6 RESPIRATORY PIGMENTS
sections.text: A respiratory pigment is a molecule that involves in transport or storage of respiratory gases. In human, haemoglobin that increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and myoglobin that stores oxygen in muscles are referred as respiratory pigments.

paras.text: A respiratory pigment is a molecule that involves in transport or storage of respiratory gases. In human, haemoglobin that increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and myoglobin that stores oxygen in muscles are referred as respiratory pigments.

sections.heading: 14.6.1 Haemoglobin:
sections.title: 14.6.1 Haemoglobin:
sections.text:
Haemoglobin is the iron-containing oxygen-transport metalloprotein in the red blood cells of almost all vertebrates. Haemoglobin in the blood carries oxygen from the respiratory organs (lungs or gills) to the rest of the body (i.e., the tissues). Here it releases the oxygen to burn nutrients to provide energy. This energy is used to power the functions of the organism, and collects the resultant carbon dioxide to bring it back to the respiratory organs to be dispensed from the organism.

paras.urdu: ہیموگلوبن تقریباً تمام فقاریوں کے سرخ خلیوں میں موجود آئرن رکھنے والی اور آکسیجن منتقل کرنے والی دھاتی پروٹین ہے۔ خون میں ہیموگلوبن تنفسی اعضا، یعنی پھیپھڑوں یا گلپھڑوں، سے آکسیجن جسم کے باقی حصوں یعنی بافتوں تک پہنچاتا ہے۔ یہاں یہ غذائی مادوں کو جلا کر توانائی حاصل کرنے کے لیے آکسیجن خارج کرتا ہے۔ یہ توانائی جاندار کے افعال چلانے میں استعمال ہوتی ہے، اور پیدا ہونے والی کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کو جمع کر کے تنفسی اعضا تک واپس لایا جاتا ہے تاکہ جسم سے خارج ہو۔
paras.pashto: هیموګلوبین د نږدې ټولو فقاریه حیواناتو د وینې په سرو حجرو کې اوسپنه لرونکی او د اکسیجن لېږدوونکی فلزي پروټین دی. په وینه کې هیموګلوبین له تنفسي غړو، یعنې سږو یا ګېلو، څخه اکسیجن د بدن نورو برخو، یعنې نسجونو، ته لېږدوي. دلته د غذایي موادو د سوځولو او انرژۍ د برابرولو لپاره اکسیجن خوشې کوي. دا انرژي د ژوندي موجود د دندو د چلولو لپاره کارول کېږي او رامنځته شوی کاربن ډای اکسایډ راټولېږي او تنفسي غړو ته بېرته راوړل کېږي، څو له بدن څخه بهر شي.

sections.heading: 14.6.2 Myoglobin
sections.title: 14.6.2 Myoglobin
sections.text:
Myoglobin (Mb) is an O₂ carrying protein that binds and releases O₂ with changes in the cytoplasm of muscle cells.

Fig:14. 11 Myoglobin

paras.text: Myoglobin (Mb) is an O₂ carrying protein that binds and releases O₂ with changes in the cytoplasm of muscle cells.

sections.heading: 14.7.1 Sinusitis:
sections.title: 14.7.1 Sinusitis:
sections.text:
Sinusitis is an inflammation of the nasal sinuses that may be acute (symptoms last 2 - 8 weeks) or chronic (symptoms last much longer). The sinuses are holes in the skull between the facial bones. There are four large sinuses: two inside the cheekbones (the maxillary sinuses) and two above the eyes (the frontal sinuses). The sinuses are lined with membranes that secrete antibody-containing mucus, which protects the respiratory passages from the irritants in the air we breathe.

Causes and Risk Factors of Sinusitis

It is usually caused by infection (bacterial or viral), but can also be caused by allergic reactions dust, pollen etc. Environmental agents, such as excessive dryness in homes and offices from dry-air heating and air-conditioning systems can also inflame the sinuses.

Fig:14. 12 Some of the symptoms of sinusitis

Symptoms of Sinusitis

The classic symptoms of acute (short lasting) sinusitis are:

fever
nasal obstruction
pus-like (purulent) nasal discharge
loss of sense of smell
facial pain or headache
Entering of nasal fluid into pharynx)

Treatment of Sinusitis

If a bacterial infection is present, antibiotics, or sulfa drugs, are usually prescribed.

Antiallergic and decongestants are also used for treatment of sinusitis.

sections.heading: 14.7.2 Otitis Media
sections.title: 14.7.2 Otitis Media
sections.text:
Otitis media is an inflammation of the middle ear. The eustachian tubes equalize the pressure between the middle ear cavity and the outside mucus to drain out of the middle ear cavity.

Inflammation of the middle ear causes the tubes to close causing the fluid to become trapped. Bacteria travel from the back of the nose through the fluid in the eustachian tube directly into the middle ear cavity and multiply in the fluid.

Fig: 14.13 Internal structure of ear showing region of middle ear.

Causes and Risk Factors of Otitis Media

Children are more commonly affected than adults because of the small size and horizontal position of their eustachian tube. The four main causes of otitis media are allergy, infection, blockage of the eustachian tube and nutritional deficiency.

Symptoms of Otitis Media

Otitis media causes

sudden, severe earache
deafness, and tinnitus (ringing or buzzing in the ear)
sense of fullness in the ear
irritability
fever, headache, a change in appetite or sleeping patterns
fluid leaking from the ear, nausea
difficulty in speaking and hearing

Occasionally, the eardrum can burst, which causes a discharge of pus and relief of pain.

For Your Information
An Otoscope or auriscope is a medical device which is used to look into the ears. Otoscope consists of a light source and a simple low-power magnifying lens.

Treatment of Otitis Media

Around 80% of cases of otitis media clear up within three or four days without treatment. Perforated eardrums also usually heal on their own without the need for treatment. However, for complicated cases, following treatment options may be taken into consideration.

Antibiotics may be prescribed to treat severe cases of middle ear infection or cases that get worse after two or three days.
Painkillers, may be used to control the main symptoms of middle ear infection (pain and fever).

For Your Information
For children with recurrent, severe middle ear infections, tiny tubes may be inserted through the eardrum to help drain fluid. These tubes are called grommets or tympanostomy tubes. Sometime a small hole is made in the eardrum surgically to allow fluid to drain out. This surgical operation is called myringotomy.

sections.heading: 14.7.3 Pneumonia
sections.title: 14.7.3 Pneumonia
sections.text:
Pneumonia is a serious disorder of lower respiratory tract which is characterized by inflammation of alveolar wall and the presence of fluid and pus in alveolar sacs of one or both lungs.

Causes and Risk Factors of Pneumonia

There are over 30 different causes of pneumonia, but usually pneumonia is caused by bacterial infection (including mycoplasma) and viruses, which can enter the body through the mouth, nose and eyes. If the body's resistance is down, the natural immunity against diseases is weakened then microorganisms are free to spread into the lungs. Thus, alveoli become filled with fluid and pus from the infectious agent, making it more difficult for the body to get the oxygen it needs, and the person may become sick.

The bacteria that cause bacterial pneumonia are Streptococcus pneumonia, Hemophilus influenzae, Legionella pneumophilia, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycoplasma.

If pneumonia is not treated timely, some complications may arise that include pleural effusion (fluid around the lung), empyema (pus in the pleural cavity), hyponatremia (low blood sodium) and rarely, an abscess in the lung.

Symptoms of Pneumonia

Symptoms vary, depending on the type of pneumonia and the individual.

With bacterial pneumonia, the person may experience shaking, chills, chattering teeth, severe chest pain, very high fever, sweating, rapid breathing, rapid pulse rate
With viral pneumonia, the person may experience fever, dry cough, headache, muscle pain and weakness. These flu-like symptoms may be followed within one or two days by increasing breathlessness, dry cough becomes worse and produces a small amount of mucus, higher fever, bluish color to the lips
With mycoplasma pneumonia, the person may experience violent coughing attacks, chills, fever, nausea, vomiting, slow heartbeat, and breathlessness, bluish color to lips and nail beds, diarrhoea and muscle aches.

Fig:14.14 In pneumonia body is unable to get proper amount of oxygen due to Fluid in the air sacs.

Treatment of Pneumonia

Treatment depends on the severity of symptoms and the type of organism causing the infection. Mostly antibiotics are prescribed.

paras.text: Pneumonia is a serious disorder of lower respiratory tract which is characterized by inflammation of alveolar wall and the presence of fluid and pus in alveolar sacs of one or both lungs.
paras.urdu: نمونیا نچلی تنفسی گزرگاہ کی سنگین بیماری ہے جس میں ہوائی تھیلوں کی دیوار کی سوزش اور ایک یا دونوں پھیپھڑوں کے ہوائی تھیلوں میں مائع اور پیپ موجود ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: نمونیا د ښکته تنفسي لارې جدي ناروغي ده چې د الویولونو د دېوال په التهاب او د یوه یا دواړو سږو په هوایي کڅوړو کې د مایع او چرک په شتون پېژندل کېږي.

paras.text: Causes and Risk Factors of Pneumonia
paras.urdu: نمونیا کے اسباب اور خطرے کے عوامل
paras.pashto: د نمونیا لاملونه او د خطر عوامل

paras.text: There are over 30 different causes of pneumonia, but usually pneumonia is caused by bacterial infection (including mycoplasma) and viruses, which can enter the body through the mouth, nose and eyes. If the body's resistance is down, the natural immunity against diseases is weakened then microorganisms are free to spread into the lungs. Thus, alveoli become filled with fluid and pus from the infectious agent, making it more difficult for the body to get the oxygen it needs, and the person may become sick.
paras.urdu: نمونیا کے 30 سے زیادہ مختلف اسباب ہیں، مگر یہ عموماً بیکٹیریا، بشمول مائکوپلازما، اور وائرس کے انفیکشن سے ہوتا ہے جو منہ، ناک اور آنکھوں سے جسم میں داخل ہو سکتے ہیں۔ اگر جسم کی مزاحمت اور بیماریوں کے خلاف قدرتی مدافعت کمزور ہو تو خرد جاندار پھیپھڑوں میں پھیل سکتے ہیں۔ یوں متعدی عامل کی وجہ سے ہوائی تھیلے مائع اور پیپ سے بھر جاتے ہیں، جسم کو مطلوبہ آکسیجن حاصل کرنا مشکل ہوتا ہے اور شخص بیمار ہو سکتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: د نمونیا له 30 څخه ډېر بېلابېل لاملونه شته، خو عموماً د باکتریاوو، د مایکوپلازما په ګډون، او ویروسونو له انتان رامنځته کېږي چې د خولې، پوزې او سترګو له لارې بدن ته ننوتلای شي. که د بدن مقاومت او د ناروغیو پر وړاندې طبیعي معافیت کمزوری وي، کوچني ژوندي موجودات په سږو کې خپرېدای شي. په دې توګه د انتاني عامل له امله الویولونه له مایع او چرک ډکېږي، بدن ته د اړین اکسیجن ترلاسه کول ستونزمن کېږي او شخص ناروغېدای شي.

paras.text: The bacteria that cause bacterial pneumonia are Streptococcus pneumonia, Hemophilus influenzae, Legionella pneumophilia, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycoplasma.
paras.urdu: بیکٹیریائی نمونیا کے عوامل Streptococcus pneumonia، Hemophilus influenzae، Legionella pneumophilia، Staphylococcus aureus اور Mycoplasma ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د باکتریايي نمونیا عوامل Streptococcus pneumonia، Hemophilus influenzae، Legionella pneumophilia، Staphylococcus aureus او Mycoplasma دي.

paras.text: If pneumonia is not treated timely, some complications may arise that include pleural effusion (fluid around the lung), empyema (pus in the pleural cavity), hyponatremia (low blood sodium) and rarely, an abscess in the lung.
paras.urdu: نمونیا کا بروقت علاج نہ ہو تو پلورل ایفیوژن، یعنی پھیپھڑے کے گرد مائع، ایمپائیما، یعنی پلورل گہا میں پیپ، ہائپوناٹریمیا، یعنی خون میں سوڈیم کی کمی، اور کبھی پھیپھڑے میں پھوڑا ہو سکتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: که د نمونیا پر وخت درملنه ونه شي، پلورايي ایفیوژن، یعنې د سږي شاوخوا مایع، ایمپایما، یعنې په پلورايي جوف کې چرک، هایپوناتریمیا، یعنې په وینه کې د سوډیم کموالی، او کله ناکله په سږي کې ابسه رامنځته کېدای شي.

paras.text: Symptoms of Pneumonia
paras.urdu: نمونیا کی علامات
paras.pashto: د نمونیا نښې

paras.text: Symptoms vary, depending on the type of pneumonia and the individual.
paras.urdu: علامات نمونیا کی قسم اور فرد کے لحاظ سے مختلف ہوتی ہیں۔
paras.pashto: نښې د نمونیا په ډول او شخص پورې اړه لري او توپیر کوي.

paras.text: With bacterial pneumonia, the person may experience shaking, chills, chattering teeth, severe chest pain, very high fever, sweating, rapid breathing, rapid pulse rate
paras.urdu: بیکٹیریائی نمونیا میں کپکپی، سردی، دانت بجنا، سینے میں شدید درد، بہت تیز بخار، پسینہ، تیز سانس اور تیز نبض ہو سکتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: په باکتریايي نمونیا کې لړزه، یخني، د غاښونو ټک ټک، سخت د سینې درد، ډېره لوړه تبه، خولې، چټکه ساه او چټک نبض رامنځته کېدای شي.

paras.text: With viral pneumonia, the person may experience fever, dry cough, headache, muscle pain and weakness. These flu-like symptoms may be followed within one or two days by increasing breathlessness, dry cough becomes worse and produces a small amount of mucus, higher fever, bluish color to the lips
paras.urdu: وائرل نمونیا میں بخار، خشک کھانسی، سر درد، عضلاتی درد اور کمزوری ہو سکتی ہے۔ فلو جیسی ان علامات کے ایک دو دن بعد سانس کی بڑھتی دشواری، بڑھتی خشک کھانسی کے ساتھ تھوڑا میوکس، زیادہ بخار اور ہونٹوں کی نیلاہٹ ہو سکتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: په ویروسي نمونیا کې تبه، وچ ټوخی، سرخوږی، د عضلو درد او کمزوري رامنځته کېدای شي. له دې زکام ته ورته نښو یوه یا دوه ورځې وروسته د ساه زیاتېدونکې ستونزه، د وچ ټوخي خرابېدل او لږ میوکس، لوړه تبه او د شونډو آبي رنګ رامنځته کېدای شي.

paras.text: With mycoplasma pneumonia, the person may experience violent coughing attacks, chills, fever, nausea, vomiting, slow heartbeat, and breathlessness, bluish color to lips and nail beds, diarrhoea and muscle aches.
paras.urdu: مائکوپلازما نمونیا میں شدید کھانسی کے دورے، سردی، بخار، متلی، قے، دل کی سست دھڑکن، سانس کی دشواری، ہونٹوں اور ناخنوں کے نیچے نیلاہٹ، اسہال اور عضلاتی درد ہو سکتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: په مایکوپلازما نمونیا کې د سخت ټوخي حملې، یخني، تبه، زړه بدوالی، کانګې، د زړه ورو ضربان، د ساه ستونزه، د شونډو او نوکانو د بېخ آبي رنګ، نس ناستی او د عضلو درد رامنځته کېدای شي.

paras.text: Fig:14.14 In pneumonia body is unable to get proper amount of oxygen due to Fluid in the air sacs.
paras.urdu: شکل 14.14: نمونیا میں ہوائی تھیلوں میں مائع کی وجہ سے جسم کو مناسب مقدار میں آکسیجن نہیں ملتی۔
paras.pashto: شکل 14.14: په نمونیا کې د هوا په کڅوړو کې د مایع له امله بدن ته مناسبه اندازه اکسیجن نه رسېږي.

paras.text: Treatment of Pneumonia
paras.urdu: نمونیا کا علاج
paras.pashto: د نمونیا درملنه

paras.text: Treatment depends on the severity of symptoms and the type of organism causing the infection. Mostly antibiotics are prescribed.
paras.urdu: علاج علامات کی شدت اور انفیکشن پیدا کرنے والے جاندار کی قسم پر منحصر ہوتا ہے۔ زیادہ تر اینٹی بایوٹک تجویز کی جاتی ہیں۔
paras.pashto: درملنه د نښو په شدت او د انتان د جوړوونکي ژوندي موجود په ډول پورې اړه لري. ډېری وخت انټي بیوټیک تجویز کېږي.

sections.heading: 14.7.4 Tuberculosis
sections.title: 14.7.4 Tuberculosis
sections.text:
Tuberculosis (TB) is a highly contagious chronic bacterial infection of lungs. TB infection begins when the mycobacteria reach the alveoli, where they invade and replicate within the phagosomes (vacuole formed as a result of phagocytosis) of alveolar macrophages, but they are unable to digest the bacterium.

Causes:

TB is caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis that is transmitted from person to person by airborne droplets. Usually this infection is passed on as a result of very close contact, so family members of an infected person are in dangered if the person continues to live in the same household and has not undergone proper treatment.

tidbit
About 15 percent of TB patients may develop the disease in an organ other than the lung, such as the lymph nodes, GI tract, bones and joints.

Risk factors for TB include the following:

HIV infection, low socioeconomic status, alcoholism, homelessness, crowded living conditions, diseases that weaken the immune system, migration from a country with a high number of cases, and health-care workers.

Symptoms of Tuberculosis

You may not notice any symptoms of illness until the disease is quite advanced. Loss of weight, loss of energy, poor appetite, fever, a productive cough, and night sweats -- might easily be blamed on another disease. Only about 10% of people infected with M. tuberculosis ever develop tuberculosis disease. Many of those who suffer TB do so in the first few years following infection, but the bacillus may lie dormant in the body for decades.

Treatment of Tuberculosis

Tuberculosis can be cured by a course of antibiotics taken over several months. Isoniazid and rifampin are the most common drugs used for TB. Inexpensive, effective and easy to take, these can prevent most cases of TB.

Fig: 14.15 Steps in the primary tuberculosis infection.

The disease can also be prevented by:

1) Vaccinating infants with BCG vaccine.
2) Isolating infectious patients.
3) Improving hygienic condition and housing.
4) Using pasteurized and properly boiled milk.

paras.urdu: تپ دق کی علامات

paras.text: You may not notice any symptoms of illness until the disease is quite advanced. Loss of weight, loss of energy, poor appetite, fever, a productive cough, and night sweats -- might easily be blamed on another disease. Only about 10% of people infected with M. tuberculosis ever develop tuberculosis disease. Many of those who suffer TB do so in the first few years following infection, but the bacillus may lie dormant in the body for decades.
paras.urdu: بیماری کافی بڑھ جانے تک ممکن ہے آپ کو کوئی علامت محسوس نہ ہو۔ وزن اور توانائی کی کمی، بھوک میں کمی، بخار، بلغم والی کھانسی اور رات کا پسینہ آسانی سے دوسری بیماری کی علامات سمجھے جا سکتے ہیں۔ M. tuberculosis سے متاثرہ لوگوں میں صرف تقریباً 10% کو کبھی تپ دق کی بیماری ہوتی ہے۔ بہت سے لوگوں میں انفیکشن کے ابتدائی چند برسوں میں TB ہوتا ہے، مگر جرثومہ جسم میں کئی دہائیوں تک غیر فعال رہ سکتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: تر دې چې ناروغي ډېره پرمختللې نه وي، کېدای شي تاسو د ناروغۍ هېڅ نښه ونه وینئ. د وزن او انرژۍ کمېدل، لږه اشتها، تبه، بلغم لرونکی ټوخی او د شپې خولې په اسانۍ د بلې ناروغۍ نښې ګڼل کېدای شي. په M. tuberculosis اخته خلکو کې یوازې نږدې 10% د نري رنځ ناروغي پیدا کوي. په ډېرو کسانو کې له انتان وروسته په لومړیو څو کلونو کې TB رامنځته کېږي، خو باسیلوس په بدن کې د لسیزو لپاره غلی پاتې کېدای شي.

paras.urdu: تپ دق کا علاج
paras.pashto: د نري رنځ درملنه

paras.text: Tuberculosis can be cured by a course of antibiotics taken over several months. Isoniazid and rifampin are the most common drugs used for TB. Inexpensive, effective and easy to take, these can prevent most cases of TB.

sections.heading: 14.8 Disorders of Lungs
sections.title: 14.8 Disorders of Lungs
sections.text:
14.8.1 Emphysema

Emphysema is a lung disease which is characterized by

shortness of breath with exertion, eventually breathlessness all the time
Coughing
Fatigue
Cyanosis (a blue tinge to the skin) due to lack of oxygen

The exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place in the small air sacs of the lungs (alveoli). In a person with emphysema, the alveoli are damaged. The main tubes leading into the lungs (the bronchi) are also damaged and narrowed. The airways of the lungs are elastic. After repeated exposure to chemical irritants, such as cigarette smoke, the alveoli and bronchioles lose their elasticity.

The movement of oxygen from the air to the blood becomes more difficult. Emphysema is generally caused by cigarette smoking or long-term exposure to certain industrial pollutants or dust.

Fig: 4.16 Emphysema results in damaging fhe bronchiole and alveoli.

paras.pashto: د اکسیجن د کموالي له امله سیانوسس، یعنې د پوستکي آبي رنګ

paras.text: The exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place in the small air sacs of the lungs (alveoli). In a person with emphysema, the alveoli are damaged. The main tubes leading into the lungs (the bronchi) are also damaged and narrowed. The airways of the lungs are elastic. After repeated exposure to chemical irritants, such as cigarette smoke, the alveoli and bronchioles lose their elasticity.
paras.urdu: آکسیجن اور کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کا تبادلہ پھیپھڑوں کے چھوٹے ہوائی تھیلوں، الویولی، میں ہوتا ہے۔ ایمفائزیما کے مریض میں ہوائی تھیلے خراب ہو جاتے ہیں۔ پھیپھڑوں کو جانے والی مرکزی نالیاں، شعبے، بھی خراب اور تنگ ہو جاتی ہیں۔ پھیپھڑوں کی ہوا کی گزرگاہیں لچک دار ہوتی ہیں۔ سگریٹ کے دھوئیں جیسے کیمیائی خراش پیدا کرنے والے مادوں سے بار بار واسطہ پڑنے پر ہوائی تھیلے اور چھوٹے شعبے اپنی لچک کھو دیتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د اکسیجن او کاربن ډای اکسایډ تبادله د سږو په کوچنیو هوایي کڅوړو، الویولونو، کې کېږي. په ایمفایزیما اخته شخص کې الویولونه زیانمن شوي وي. سږو ته تلونکي اصلي نلونه، برانشونه، هم زیانمن او تنګ شوي وي. د سږو د هوا لارې ارتجاعي دي. له کیمیاوي تحریکوونکو، لکه د سګرېټ لوګي، سره په بیا بیا مخ کېدو الویولونه او برانشیولونه خپل ارتجاعي خاصیت له لاسه ورکوي.

paras.text: The movement of oxygen from the air to the blood becomes more difficult. Emphysema is generally caused by cigarette smoking or long-term exposure to certain industrial pollutants or dust.
paras.urdu: ہوا سے خون میں آکسیجن کا جانا زیادہ مشکل ہو جاتا ہے۔ ایمفائزیما عموماً سگریٹ نوشی یا بعض صنعتی آلودگیوں اور گرد سے طویل مدت تک واسطے سے ہوتا ہے۔
paras.pashto: له هوا څخه وینې ته د اکسیجن تګ ډېر ستونزمن کېږي. ایمفایزیما عموماً د سګرېټ څکولو یا له ځینو صنعتي ککړوونکو او دوړو سره د اوږدمهاله مخ کېدو له امله وي.

sections.heading: 14.8.2 Lung cancer
sections.title: 14.8.2 Lung cancer
sections.text:
Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in the world. Cigarette smoking is one of the major causes of most lung cancers. The more cigarettes you smoke per day and the earlier you started smoking, the greater is the risk of lung cancer. High levels of pollution, radiation and asbestos exposure may also increase risk.

Common symptoms of lung cancer include

A cough that doesn't go away and gets worse over time
Constant chest pain
Coughing up blood
Shortness of breath,
Repeated problems with pneumonia or bronchitis
Swelling of the neck and face
Loss of appetite or weight loss
Fatigue

There are many types of lung cancer. Each type of lung cancer grows and spreads in different ways and is treated differently. Treatment also depends on the stage, or how advanced it is. Treatment may include chemotherapy, radiation and surgery.

Fig: 4.17 Tumor in the lungs can develop at any place causing lung cancer.

sections.heading: 14.8.3 Effects of smoking on the respiratory system
sections.title: 14.8.3 Effects of smoking on the respiratory system
sections.headingUrdu: تنفسی نظام پر سگریٹ نوشی کے اثرات
sections.headingPashto: پر تنفسي سیسټم د سګرېټ څکولو اغېزې
sections.urduTitle: تنفسی نظام پر سگریٹ نوشی کے اثرات
sections.text:
The effects of tobacco smoke on the respiratory system include:

Irritation of the trachea (windpipe) and larynx (voice box)
Reduced lung function and breathlessness due to swelling and narrowing of the lung airways and excess mucus in the lung passages
Impairment of the lungs' clearance system, leading to the build-up of poisonous substances, which results in lung irritation and damage
Increased risk of lung infection and symptoms such as coughing and wheezing
Permanent damage to the air sacs of the lungs.

sections.heading: KEY POINTS
sections.title: KEY POINTS
sections.text:
For effective diffusion the respiratory surface must be permeable, thin, possess a large surface area with good blood supply and good ventilation mechanism to maintain a steep diffusion gradient across the respiratory surface.
Respiratory system consists of nose and nasal cavities, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli in the lungs.
Lung volumes and lung capacities refer to the volume of air associated with different phases of the respiratory cycle.
Normally breathing is an involuntary process and is not controlled consciously. However, some voluntary control is also possible. During voluntary control impulses originate from the cerebral hemispheres and pass to the breathing centre.
Breathing consists of two phases namely breathing in or inspiration and breathing out or expiration.
The blood transports oxygen from the lungs to different tissues and carbon dioxides from tissues to the lungs. Approximately 97% of oxygen is carried by the red blood cells as oxyhaemoglobin, while 3% is transported as dissolved oxygen in the plasma.
Carbon dioxide is transported in the blood in three main ways i.e. in the form of bicarbonate ions, in the form of carboxyhaemoglobin and dissolved in plasma.
Approximately 70% of carbon dioxide is carried in the blood as bicarbonate ions.
About 23% of carbon dioxide is carried as carboxyhaemoglobin
Only 7% of carbon dioxide by the plasma.
In human, haemoglobin that increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and myoglobin that stores oxygen in muscles are referred as respiratory pigments.
Sinusitis is an inflammation of the nasal sinuses and it is usually caused by infection (bacterial or viral), but can also be caused by allergic reactions dust, pollen etc.
Otitis media is an inflammation of the middle ear.
Pneumonia is a serious disorder of lower respiratory tract which is characterized by inflammation of alveolar wall and the presence of fluid and pus in alveolar sacs of one or both lungs.
Tuberculosis begins when the mycobacteria reach the alveoli, where they invade and replicate within the phagosomes of alveolar macrophages, but they are unable to digest the bacterium.
Emphysema is a lung disease in which the alveoli are damaged. It is generally caused by cigarette smoking or long-term exposure to certain industrial pollutants or dust.
Lung cancer grows and spreads in different ways and its treatment depends on the stage, or how advanced it is. Treatment may include chemotherapy, radiation and surgery.

paras.text: For effective diffusion the respiratory surface must be permeable, thin, possess a large surface area with good blood supply and good ventilation mechanism to maintain a steep diffusion gradient across the respiratory surface.
paras.urdu: مؤثر انتشار کے لیے تنفسی سطح نفوذ پذیر، پتلی، بڑے رقبے والی، اچھی خون رسانی اور ہوا داری والی ہونی چاہیے تاکہ سطح کے دونوں طرف انتشار کا تیز ارتکازی فرق قائم رہے۔
paras.pashto: د اغېزمن خپرېدو لپاره تنفسي سطحه باید د تېرېدو وړ، نرۍ، پراخه او د وینې او هوا ښه رسونه لرونکې وي، څو د سطحې په دواړو خواوو کې لوی غلظتي توپیر وساتل شي.

paras.text: Respiratory system consists of nose and nasal cavities, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli in the lungs.
paras.urdu: تنفسی نظام ناک، ناک کی گہاوں، حلق، حنجرے، ہوا کی نالی، شعبوں، چھوٹے شعبوں اور پھیپھڑوں کے ہوائی تھیلوں پر مشتمل ہے۔
paras.pashto: تنفسي سیسټم له پوزې، د پوزې له جوفونو، حلق، حنجرې، د هوا نل، برانشونو، برانشیولونو او د سږو له الویولونو جوړ دی.

paras.text: Lung volumes and lung capacities refer to the volume of air associated with different phases of the respiratory cycle.
paras.urdu: پھیپھڑوں کے حجم اور گنجائش تنفسی چکر کے مختلف مراحل سے متعلق ہوا کے حجم کو کہتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د سږو حجمونه او ظرفیتونه د تنفسي دورې له بېلابېلو پړاوونو سره تړلي د هوا حجم ته ویل کېږي.

paras.text: Normally breathing is an involuntary process and is not controlled consciously. However, some voluntary control is also possible. During voluntary control impulses originate from the cerebral hemispheres and pass to the breathing centre.
paras.urdu: عموماً سانس غیر ارادی عمل ہے اور شعوری طور پر کنٹرول نہیں ہوتا۔ تاہم کچھ ارادی کنٹرول بھی ممکن ہے۔ ارادی کنٹرول میں عصبی پیغامات دماغ کے نصف کروں سے تنفسی مرکز تک جاتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: په عادي ډول ساه اخیستل غیر ارادي پروسه ده او په شعوري ډول نه کنټرولېږي. خو یو څه ارادي کنټرول هم ممکن دی. په ارادي کنټرول کې عصبي پیغامونه د لوی دماغ له نیمکرو څخه تنفسي مرکز ته ځي.

paras.text: Breathing consists of two phases namely breathing in or inspiration and breathing out or expiration.
paras.urdu: سانس کے دو مراحل ہیں: سانس اندر لینا، یعنی دم، اور باہر نکالنا، یعنی بازدم۔
paras.pashto: ساه اخیستل دوه پړاوونه لري: د ساه دننه اخیستل او بهر ایستل.

paras.text: The blood transports oxygen from the lungs to different tissues and carbon dioxides from tissues to the lungs. Approximately 97% of oxygen is carried by the red blood cells as oxyhaemoglobin, while 3% is transported as dissolved oxygen in the plasma.
paras.urdu: خون آکسیجن کو پھیپھڑوں سے بافتوں اور کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کو بافتوں سے پھیپھڑوں تک لے جاتا ہے۔ تقریباً 97% آکسیجن سرخ خلیوں میں آکسی ہیموگلوبن اور 3% پلازما میں حل شدہ حالت میں منتقل ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: وینه اکسیجن له سږو نسجونو ته او کاربن ډای اکسایډ له نسجونو سږو ته لېږدوي. نږدې 97% اکسیجن د وینې په سرو حجرو کې د اکسي هیموګلوبین او 3% په پلازما کې په حل شوي حالت لېږدول کېږي.

paras.text: Carbon dioxide is transported in the blood in three main ways i.e. in the form of bicarbonate ions, in the form of carboxyhaemoglobin and dissolved in plasma.
paras.urdu: کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ خون میں تین بنیادی صورتوں میں منتقل ہوتی ہے: بائی کاربونیٹ آئن، کاربوکسی ہیموگلوبن اور پلازما میں حل شدہ حالت۔
paras.pashto: کاربن ډای اکسایډ په وینه کې په دریو اصلي بڼو لېږدول کېږي: د بای کاربونېټ ایونونه، کاربوکسي هیموګلوبین او په پلازما کې حل شوی حالت.

paras.text: Approximately 70% of carbon dioxide is carried in the blood as bicarbonate ions.
paras.urdu: تقریباً 70% کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ خون میں بائی کاربونیٹ آئنوں کی صورت میں منتقل ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: نږدې 70% کاربن ډای اکسایډ په وینه کې د بای کاربونېټ ایونونو په بڼه لېږدول کېږي.

paras.text: About 23% of carbon dioxide is carried as carboxyhaemoglobin
paras.urdu: تقریباً 23% کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کاربوکسی ہیموگلوبن کی صورت میں منتقل ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: نږدې 23% کاربن ډای اکسایډ د کاربوکسي هیموګلوبین په بڼه لېږدول کېږي.

paras.text: Only 7% of carbon dioxide by the plasma.
paras.urdu: کاربن ڈائی آکسائیڈ کی صرف 7% پلازما کے ذریعے۔
paras.pashto: د کاربن ډای اکسایډ یوازې 7% د پلازما له لارې.

paras.text: In human, haemoglobin that increases the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood and myoglobin that stores oxygen in muscles are referred as respiratory pigments.
paras.urdu: انسان میں خون کی آکسیجن لے جانے کی گنجائش بڑھانے والا ہیموگلوبن اور عضلات میں آکسیجن ذخیرہ کرنے والا میوگلوبن تنفسی رنگ دار مادے کہلاتے ہیں۔
paras.pashto: په انسان کې هیموګلوبین چې د وینې د اکسیجن د لېږد ظرفیت زیاتوي او میوګلوبین چې په عضلو کې اکسیجن ساتي، تنفسي رنګیزې مادې بلل کېږي.

paras.text: Sinusitis is an inflammation of the nasal sinuses and it is usually caused by infection (bacterial or viral), but can also be caused by allergic reactions dust, pollen etc.
paras.urdu: سائنوسائٹس ناک کے سائنَس کی سوزش ہے جو عموماً بیکٹیریائی یا وائرل انفیکشن سے ہوتی ہے، مگر گرد، زرگل وغیرہ سے الرجی کے ردِعمل سے بھی ہو سکتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: ساینوسایټس د پوزې د سینوسونو التهاب دی چې عموماً د باکتریايي یا ویروسي انتان له امله وي، خو د دوړو، ګلګردې او نورو موادو د حساسیت له غبرګونونو هم رامنځته کېدای شي.

paras.text: Otitis media is an inflammation of the middle ear.
paras.urdu: اوٹائٹس میڈیا درمیانی کان کی سوزش ہے۔
paras.pashto: اوټایټس مېډیا د منځني غوږ التهاب دی.

paras.text: Pneumonia is a serious disorder of lower respiratory tract which is characterized by inflammation of alveolar wall and the presence of fluid and pus in alveolar sacs of one or both lungs.
paras.urdu: نمونیا نچلی تنفسی گزرگاہ کی سنگین بیماری ہے جس میں ہوائی تھیلوں کی دیوار کی سوزش اور ایک یا دونوں پھیپھڑوں کے ہوائی تھیلوں میں مائع اور پیپ ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: نمونیا د ښکته تنفسي لارې جدي ناروغي ده چې د الویولونو د دېوال په التهاب او د یوه یا دواړو سږو په کڅوړو کې د مایع او چرک په شتون پېژندل کېږي.

paras.text: Tuberculosis begins when the mycobacteria reach the alveoli, where they invade and replicate within the phagosomes of alveolar macrophages, but they are unable to digest the bacterium.
paras.urdu: تپ دق اس وقت شروع ہوتا ہے جب مائکوبیکٹیریا ہوائی تھیلوں تک پہنچ کر الویولر میکروفیج کے فیگوسوم میں داخل ہوتے اور بڑھتے ہیں، مگر یہ خلیے بیکٹیریا کو ہضم نہیں کر سکتے۔
paras.pashto: نری رنځ هغه وخت پیلېږي چې مایکوباکتریاوې الویولونو ته ورسېږي او د الویولي ماکروفاژونو په فاګوسومونو کې ننوځي او ډېرېږي، خو دا حجرې باکتریا نه شي هضمولای.

paras.text: Emphysema is a lung disease in which the alveoli are damaged. It is generally caused by cigarette smoking or long-term exposure to certain industrial pollutants or dust.
paras.urdu: ایمفائزیما پھیپھڑوں کی بیماری ہے جس میں ہوائی تھیلے خراب ہوتے ہیں۔ یہ عموماً سگریٹ نوشی یا بعض صنعتی آلودگیوں اور گرد سے طویل واسطے سے ہوتی ہے۔
paras.pashto: ایمفایزیما د سږو ناروغي ده چې الویولونه په کې زیانمن کېږي. دا عموماً د سګرېټ څکولو یا له ځینو صنعتي ککړوونکو او دوړو سره د اوږدمهاله مخ کېدو له امله وي.

paras.text: Lung cancer grows and spreads in different ways and its treatment depends on the stage, or how advanced it is. Treatment may include chemotherapy, radiation and surgery.
paras.urdu: پھیپھڑوں کا سرطان مختلف طریقوں سے بڑھتا اور پھیلتا ہے اور علاج اس کے مرحلے پر منحصر ہوتا ہے۔ علاج میں کیموتھراپی، تابکاری اور جراحی شامل ہو سکتی ہیں۔
paras.pashto: د سږو سرطان په بېلابېلو طریقو وده کوي او خپرېږي او درملنه یې د ناروغۍ په پړاو پورې اړه لري. په درملنه کې کیموتراپي، وړانګې او جراحي شاملېدای شي.

mcqs.q: The wall of the trachea (windpipe) and bronchi of man is furnished with a series of incomplete:
mcqs.explanation: Incomplete cartilaginous rings support the trachea and the larger bronchi while keeping their lumen open. Smaller bronchi have cartilage plates.

mcqs.q: What does not happen during inspiration in man?
mcqs.explanation: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens. Its dome-shaped relaxed position is associated with expiration.

mcqs.q: The lateral walls of the chest cavity of man are composed of the:
mcqs.explanation: The ribs and intercostal muscles form the side walls. The diaphragm forms the floor rather than the lateral walls.

mcqs.q: When the human blood leaves the capillary bed of the tissue, most of the carbon dioxide is in the form of:
mcqs.explanation: The textbook assigns about 70% of carbon dioxide transport to bicarbonate ions, the largest fraction.

mcqs.q: Which sequence of organs is correct in air passageway of man?
opts: nasal cavities larynx pharynx trachea bronchi
nasal cavities pharynx trachea larynx bronchi
nasal cavities pharynx larynx bronchi trachea
nasal cavities pharynx larynx trachea bronchi
mcqs.explanation: Air passes from the nasal cavities to the pharynx, larynx, trachea and then the bronchi.

mcqs.q: Which part of the air passage way possesses cartilage plates in its wall?
mcqs.explanation: Cartilage is arranged as plates in the smaller, more distal bronchi. The trachea and proximal bronchi have ring supports; bronchioles lack cartilage.

mcqs.q: Human lungs are spongy due to the presence of million of:
mcqs.explanation: The numerous small air sacs, alveoli, contribute to the spongy structure of lung tissue.

mcqs.q: Which event is not associated with the activity of expiration?
opts: more dome like shape of diaphragm
back ward & down ward movement of rib cage
mcqs.explanation: Quiet expiration follows relaxation of the diaphragm and intercostal muscles. Diaphragm contraction initiates inspiration.

mcqs.q: Oxygen carrying capacity of blood does not depend upon:
mcqs.explanation: For carrying capacity expressed per fixed blood volume, the total quantity of blood is not the determining factor. Oxygen pressure, altitude and carbon-dioxide-related changes affect loading; haemoglobin concentration also matters.

mcqs.q: When haemoglobin of the blood is fully saturated with oxygen, the 100cc of blood contains.
mcqs.explanation: The textbook gives a maximum of about 20 ml oxygen per 100 ml blood; 1 cc equals 1 ml.

shortQuestions.q: What are the risk factors and causes of TB?
steps: Identify the cause: infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Explain transmission: infectious airborne droplets can pass between people, especially during close or prolonged contact.
List risk factors from the chapter: HIV or weakened immunity, poverty, crowded housing, homelessness, alcoholism, migration from a country with many cases, and health-care exposure.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Identify the cause: infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
  2. Explain transmission: infectious airborne droplets can pass between people, especially during close or prolonged contact.
  3. List risk factors from the chapter: HIV or weakened immunity, poverty, crowded housing, homelessness, alcoholism, migration from a country with many cases, and health-care exposure.
Answer: TB is caused by M. tuberculosis; close exposure and conditions that increase exposure or weaken immunity raise the risk.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: TB is caused by M. tuberculosis; close exposure and conditions that increase exposure or weaken immunity raise the risk.

shortQuestions.q: State the signs and symptoms of otitis media.
steps: Start with the ear symptoms: sudden severe earache, hearing loss, tinnitus and fullness in the ear.
Add the general symptoms: irritability, fever, headache, appetite or sleeping changes and nausea.
Include fluid discharge and difficulty speaking or hearing; a ruptured eardrum may discharge pus and reduce pain.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Start with the ear symptoms: sudden severe earache, hearing loss, tinnitus and fullness in the ear.
  2. Add the general symptoms: irritability, fever, headache, appetite or sleeping changes and nausea.
  3. Include fluid discharge and difficulty speaking or hearing; a ruptured eardrum may discharge pus and reduce pain.
Answer: Ear pain, hearing disturbance, fullness, fever or irritability and possible ear discharge are the listed signs and symptoms.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Ear pain, hearing disturbance, fullness, fever or irritability and possible ear discharge are the listed signs and symptoms.

shortQuestions.q: List two differences between haemoglobin and myoglobin.
steps: Compare location: haemoglobin is in red blood cells; myoglobin is in muscle cells.
Compare function: haemoglobin transports oxygen in blood; myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles and releases it when needed.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Compare location: haemoglobin is in red blood cells; myoglobin is in muscle cells.
  2. Compare function: haemoglobin transports oxygen in blood; myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles and releases it when needed.
Answer: Haemoglobin: red blood cells and oxygen transport. Myoglobin: muscle cells and oxygen storage.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Haemoglobin: red blood cells and oxygen transport. Myoglobin: muscle cells and oxygen storage.

shortQuestions.q: Give any two factors that affect the oxygen carrying capacity of blood.
steps: Choose haemoglobin concentration: more functioning haemoglobin per fixed blood volume provides more oxygen-binding sites.
Choose oxygen partial pressure: it affects haemoglobin oxygen loading and saturation.
Distinguish maximum capacity from the oxygen actually carried at a particular saturation.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Choose haemoglobin concentration: more functioning haemoglobin per fixed blood volume provides more oxygen-binding sites.
  2. Choose oxygen partial pressure: it affects haemoglobin oxygen loading and saturation.
  3. Distinguish maximum capacity from the oxygen actually carried at a particular saturation.
Answer: Haemoglobin concentration and oxygen partial pressure affect oxygen carriage.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Haemoglobin concentration and oxygen partial pressure affect oxygen carriage.

longQuestions.q: Describe the structure of human respiratory system.
steps: Follow the air path: nostrils and nasal cavities → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
Describe the nose: hairs, mucus and cilia filter air; a blood supply warms it and mucus moistens it.
Describe the conducting passages: pharynx is shared with the digestive tract; the larynx has vocal cords; cartilage supports the trachea and bronchi.
Describe the branching passages: two bronchi enter the lungs, divide repeatedly and form bronchioles, which lack cartilage and open into alveoli.
Describe the exchange surfaces: thin moist alveolar epithelium, capillary networks and a large area support diffusion; elastic fibres allow expansion and recoil.
Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Follow the air path: nostrils and nasal cavities → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
  2. Describe the nose: hairs, mucus and cilia filter air; a blood supply warms it and mucus moistens it.
  3. Describe the conducting passages: pharynx is shared with the digestive tract; the larynx has vocal cords; cartilage supports the trachea and bronchi.
  4. Describe the branching passages: two bronchi enter the lungs, divide repeatedly and form bronchioles, which lack cartilage and open into alveoli.
  5. Describe the exchange surfaces: thin moist alveolar epithelium, capillary networks and a large area support diffusion; elastic fibres allow expansion and recoil.
  6. Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.
Answer: The respiratory system combines conducting air passages with alveolar gas-exchange surfaces inside the paired lungs.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: The respiratory system combines conducting air passages with alveolar gas-exchange surfaces inside the paired lungs.

longQuestions.q: Describe the mechanism of breathing in man.
steps: Identify the control system: medullary respiratory centres send rhythmic signals through intercostal and phrenic nerves.
In inspiration the external intercostal muscles contract and the ribs move upward and outward; the diaphragm contracts and flattens.
Thoracic volume increases, pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure, and air enters through the air passages.
During quiet expiration the muscles relax; the diaphragm becomes dome-shaped and the ribs move down and inward.
Elastic recoil reduces lung volume, pressure rises, and air flows outward; forced expiration recruits additional muscular effort.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Identify the control system: medullary respiratory centres send rhythmic signals through intercostal and phrenic nerves.
  2. In inspiration the external intercostal muscles contract and the ribs move upward and outward; the diaphragm contracts and flattens.
  3. Thoracic volume increases, pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure, and air enters through the air passages.
  4. During quiet expiration the muscles relax; the diaphragm becomes dome-shaped and the ribs move down and inward.
  5. Elastic recoil reduces lung volume, pressure rises, and air flows outward; forced expiration recruits additional muscular effort.
Answer: Breathing alternates pressure changes produced by ribs, respiratory muscles and diaphragm, causing air to move into and out of the lungs.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Breathing alternates pressure changes produced by ribs, respiratory muscles and diaphragm, causing air to move into and out of the lungs.

longQuestions.q: Describe the role of respiratory pigments in transport and storage of respiratory gases.
steps: Define respiratory pigments as molecules involved in respiratory-gas transport or storage.
Explain haemoglobin: its iron-containing haem groups bind oxygen reversibly; one molecule can bind four oxygen molecules.
High oxygen partial pressure in the lungs favours loading, while tissue conditions favour unloading.
Explain carbon-dioxide carriage: some binds to globin as carbaminohaemoglobin; most is carried as bicarbonate, and haemoglobin helps buffer hydrogen ions.
Explain myoglobin: it binds and stores oxygen in muscle cells, making oxygen available during demand.
Give other source examples: haemocyanin in molluscs, haemoerythrin in some marine animals and chlorocruorin in annelids.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Define respiratory pigments as molecules involved in respiratory-gas transport or storage.
  2. Explain haemoglobin: its iron-containing haem groups bind oxygen reversibly; one molecule can bind four oxygen molecules.
  3. High oxygen partial pressure in the lungs favours loading, while tissue conditions favour unloading.
  4. Explain carbon-dioxide carriage: some binds to globin as carbaminohaemoglobin; most is carried as bicarbonate, and haemoglobin helps buffer hydrogen ions.
  5. Explain myoglobin: it binds and stores oxygen in muscle cells, making oxygen available during demand.
  6. Give other source examples: haemocyanin in molluscs, haemoerythrin in some marine animals and chlorocruorin in annelids.
Answer: Haemoglobin chiefly transports oxygen in blood and assists carbon-dioxide transport and buffering; myoglobin supplies muscle oxygen storage.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Haemoglobin chiefly transports oxygen in blood and assists carbon-dioxide transport and buffering; myoglobin supplies muscle oxygen storage.

longQuestions.q: State the causes, symptoms, and treatment of any one disorder of lower respiratory tract.
steps: Choose the textbook example pneumonia and define it as inflammation with fluid or pus in alveolar sacs.
State causes from the chapter: bacterial infection, including mycoplasma, or viral infection.
State symptoms: cough, fever, chest pain, breathing difficulty and weakness; exact combinations vary with the agent.
Describe textbook treatment generally: treatment depends on severity and the infecting organism; antibacterial medicines address bacterial infection.
State complications listed in the chapter: pleural effusion, empyema, hyponatraemia and rarely lung abscess.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Choose the textbook example pneumonia and define it as inflammation with fluid or pus in alveolar sacs.
  2. State causes from the chapter: bacterial infection, including mycoplasma, or viral infection.

mcqs.q: The wall of the trachea (windpipe) and bronchi of man is furnished with a series of incomplete:
mcqs.explanation: Incomplete cartilaginous rings support the trachea and the larger bronchi while keeping their lumen open. Smaller bronchi have cartilage plates.

mcqs.q: What does not happen during inspiration in man?
mcqs.explanation: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens. Its dome-shaped relaxed position is associated with expiration.

mcqs.q: The lateral walls of the chest cavity of man are composed of the:
mcqs.explanation: The ribs and intercostal muscles form the side walls. The diaphragm forms the floor rather than the lateral walls.

mcqs.q: When the human blood leaves the capillary bed of the tissue, most of the carbon dioxide is in the form of:
mcqs.explanation: The textbook assigns about 70% of carbon dioxide transport to bicarbonate ions, the largest fraction.

mcqs.q: Which sequence of organs is correct in air passageway of man?
opts: nasal cavities larynx pharynx trachea bronchi
nasal cavities pharynx trachea larynx bronchi
nasal cavities pharynx larynx bronchi trachea
nasal cavities pharynx larynx trachea bronchi
mcqs.explanation: Air passes from the nasal cavities to the pharynx, larynx, trachea and then the bronchi.

mcqs.q: Which part of the air passage way possesses cartilage plates in its wall?
mcqs.explanation: Cartilage is arranged as plates in the smaller, more distal bronchi. The trachea and proximal bronchi have ring supports; bronchioles lack cartilage.

mcqs.q: Human lungs are spongy due to the presence of million of:
mcqs.explanation: The numerous small air sacs, alveoli, contribute to the spongy structure of lung tissue.

mcqs.q: Which event is not associated with the activity of expiration?
opts: more dome like shape of diaphragm
back ward & down ward movement of rib cage
mcqs.explanation: Quiet expiration follows relaxation of the diaphragm and intercostal muscles. Diaphragm contraction initiates inspiration.

mcqs.q: Oxygen carrying capacity of blood does not depend upon:
mcqs.explanation: For carrying capacity expressed per fixed blood volume, the total quantity of blood is not the determining factor. Oxygen pressure, altitude and carbon-dioxide-related changes affect loading; haemoglobin concentration also matters.

mcqs.q: When haemoglobin of the blood is fully saturated with oxygen, the 100cc of blood contains.
mcqs.explanation: The textbook gives a maximum of about 20 ml oxygen per 100 ml blood; 1 cc equals 1 ml.

shortQuestions.q: List two differences between haemoglobin and myoglobin.
steps: Compare location: haemoglobin is in red blood cells; myoglobin is in muscle cells.
Compare function: haemoglobin transports oxygen in blood; myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles and releases it when needed.

SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Compare location: haemoglobin is in red blood cells; myoglobin is in muscle cells.
  2. Compare function: haemoglobin transports oxygen in blood; myoglobin stores oxygen in muscles and releases it when needed.
Answer: Haemoglobin: red blood cells and oxygen transport. Myoglobin: muscle cells and oxygen storage.
shortQuestions.plainAnswer: Haemoglobin: red blood cells and oxygen transport. Myoglobin: muscle cells and oxygen storage.

shortQuestions.q: Give any two factors that affect the oxygen carrying capacity of blood.
steps: Choose haemoglobin concentration: more functioning haemoglobin per fixed blood volume provides more oxygen-binding sites.
Choose oxygen partial pressure: it affects haemoglobin oxygen loading and saturation.
Distinguish maximum capacity from the oxygen actually carried at a particular saturation.
shortQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer

  2. Choose oxygen partial pressure: it affects haemoglobin oxygen loading and saturation.
  3. Distinguish maximum capacity from the oxygen actually carried at a particular saturation.
Answer: Haemoglobin concentration and oxygen partial pressure affect oxygen carriage.

longQuestions.q: Describe the structure of human respiratory system.
steps: Follow the air path: nostrils and nasal cavities → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
Describe the nose: hairs, mucus and cilia filter air; a blood supply warms it and mucus moistens it.
Describe the conducting passages: pharynx is shared with the digestive tract; the larynx has vocal cords; cartilage supports the trachea and bronchi.
Describe the branching passages: two bronchi enter the lungs, divide repeatedly and form bronchioles, which lack cartilage and open into alveoli.
Describe the exchange surfaces: thin moist alveolar epithelium, capillary networks and a large area support diffusion; elastic fibres allow expansion and recoil.
Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Follow the air path: nostrils and nasal cavities → pharynx → larynx → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
  2. Describe the nose: hairs, mucus and cilia filter air; a blood supply warms it and mucus moistens it.
  3. Describe the conducting passages: pharynx is shared with the digestive tract; the larynx has vocal cords; cartilage supports the trachea and bronchi.
  4. Describe the branching passages: two bronchi enter the lungs, divide repeatedly and form bronchioles, which lack cartilage and open into alveoli.
  5. Describe the exchange surfaces: thin moist alveolar epithelium, capillary networks and a large area support diffusion; elastic fibres allow expansion and recoil.
  6. Locate the lungs: the right has three lobes, the left two; pleural membranes surround them and their bases rest on the diaphragm.
Answer: The respiratory system combines conducting air passages with alveolar gas-exchange surfaces inside the paired lungs.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: The respiratory system combines conducting air passages with alveolar gas-exchange surfaces inside the paired lungs.

longQuestions.q: Describe the mechanism of breathing in man.
steps: Identify the control system: medullary respiratory centres send rhythmic signals through intercostal and phrenic nerves.
In inspiration the external intercostal muscles contract and the ribs move upward and outward; the diaphragm contracts and flattens.
Thoracic volume increases, pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure, and air enters through the air passages.
During quiet expiration the muscles relax; the diaphragm becomes dome-shaped and the ribs move down and inward.
Elastic recoil reduces lung volume, pressure rises, and air flows outward; forced expiration recruits additional muscular effort.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Identify the control system: medullary respiratory centres send rhythmic signals through intercostal and phrenic nerves.
  2. In inspiration the external intercostal muscles contract and the ribs move upward and outward; the diaphragm contracts and flattens.
  3. Thoracic volume increases, pressure in the lungs falls below atmospheric pressure, and air enters through the air passages.
  4. During quiet expiration the muscles relax; the diaphragm becomes dome-shaped and the ribs move down and inward.
  5. Elastic recoil reduces lung volume, pressure rises, and air flows outward; forced expiration recruits additional muscular effort.
Answer: Breathing alternates pressure changes produced by ribs, respiratory muscles and diaphragm, causing air to move into and out of the lungs.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Breathing alternates pressure changes produced by ribs, respiratory muscles and diaphragm, causing air to move into and out of the lungs.

longQuestions.q: Describe the role of respiratory pigments in transport and storage of respiratory gases.
steps: Define respiratory pigments as molecules involved in respiratory-gas transport or storage.
Explain haemoglobin: its iron-containing haem groups bind oxygen reversibly; one molecule can bind four oxygen molecules.
High oxygen partial pressure in the lungs favours loading, while tissue conditions favour unloading.
Explain carbon-dioxide carriage: some binds to globin as carbaminohaemoglobin; most is carried as bicarbonate, and haemoglobin helps buffer hydrogen ions.
Explain myoglobin: it binds and stores oxygen in muscle cells, making oxygen available during demand.
Give other source examples: haemocyanin in molluscs, haemoerythrin in some marine animals and chlorocruorin in annelids.
longQuestions.answer:
SpaceBook learning answer
  1. Define respiratory pigments as molecules involved in respiratory-gas transport or storage.
  2. Explain haemoglobin: its iron-containing haem groups bind oxygen reversibly; one molecule can bind four oxygen molecules.
  3. High oxygen partial pressure in the lungs favours loading, while tissue conditions favour unloading.
  4. Explain carbon-dioxide carriage: some binds to globin as carbaminohaemoglobin; most is carried as bicarbonate, and haemoglobin helps buffer hydrogen ions.
  5. Explain myoglobin: it binds and stores oxygen in muscle cells, making oxygen available during demand.
  6. Give other source examples: haemocyanin in molluscs, haemoerythrin in some marine animals and chlorocruorin in annelids.
Answer: Haemoglobin chiefly transports oxygen in blood and assists carbon-dioxide transport and buffering; myoglobin supplies muscle oxygen storage.
longQuestions.plainAnswer: Haemoglobin chiefly transports oxygen in blood and assists carbon-dioxide transport and buffering; myoglobin supplies muscle oxygen storage.
